summary: Hideaki Nakatani is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at Kyoto University under Gadjin Nagao, was a disciple of Yutaka Ochihara, earned a PhD from Sorbonne Nouvelle University, and was a professor at Kobe Gakuin University (attested 2003).
Hidehiko Kurita works in religious studies and Japanology. He completed a PhD at Tohoku University and served as a lecturer at Aichi Prefectural University (attested 2020).

Hidehiro Okada (1931–2017) was a historian specializing in Iranian and Central Asian studies and Sinology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and under Nicholas Poppe at the University of Washington, later holding posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies and Tokiwa University.
Hideki Kiyoshima (born 1951) is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Delhi and served as a lecturer at Kindai University around 1989.
Hidemasa Nagata (1933–2024) specialized in history, archaeology, and Sinology. He studied at Kyoto University from circa 1952 to 1961 and served on its faculty from circa 1968 to 1997.

Hidenaka Tanaka (1886–1974) was a linguist who studied at the University of Tokyo under Raphael von Koeber, the University of Oxford, and Kyoto University. He taught at the University of Tokyo, Kyoto University, and Kyoto Women's University.

Hidenori Kitagawa (1920–1978) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under Hakuju Ui. He was a Rockefeller Foundation fellow (1952–1953) and professor at Nagoya University (attested 1968–1969).

Hidenori S. Sakuma (born 1954) specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and under Lambert Schmithausen at the University of Hamburg (PhD), later holding posts at Shitennoji University, Otani University, Taisho University, and the University of Tsukuba.

Hideo Mineshima (1927–2013) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Taisho University and Waseda University. He was a longtime professor at Waseda University (1968–1998) and later taught at Bunkyo Gakuin University.

Hideomi Yaita (born 1953) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Taisho University, served as a research assistant at the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (~1989), and was a lecturer at Taisho University (attested 1995).
Hidetaka Fukazawa (born 1956) works in religious studies. He studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies from 1975 to 1979 and held a post at Hitotsubashi University from circa 1992 to 2021.
Hidetaka Nakatani is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Kyoto University in 1966 under Gadjin Nagao.

Hideto Ono (born 1944) specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Komazawa University from 1963 to 1967 and was an associate professor at Aichi Gakuin University from circa 1988 to 1994.

Hidetoshi Yoshizawa works in Buddhist studies. He has been affiliated with Taisho University and its Comprehensive Buddhist Studies Institute, serving as a researcher, lecturer, and chief research fellow between 1998 and 2017.

Hidetsugu Yagi (1886–1976) studied at the University of Tokyo (~1906–1909) and later held academic posts at Tohoku University, Osaka University, Tokyo Institute of Technology, and the University of Tokyo.

Hideyo Ogawa (born 1954) is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He served as an associate professor (~1987–1997) and professor of Indian philosophy (~1997–2020, attested 2026) at Hiroshima University.

Hideyuki Matsumori specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He was a doctoral student at Soka University (attested 2006) and later became an assistant professor (attested 2015) and professor (attested 2026) there.

Hilko Wiardo Schomerus (1879–1945) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied under Paul Deussen at Kiel and Nathan Söderblom at Leipzig, later holding professorships at Kiel University and the University of Halle-Wittenberg.

Himanshu Prabha Ray (born 1947) is an Indologist and historian who studied at Panjab University, Cambridge, and Jawaharlal Nehru University. She taught at JNU (1980–2012) and held appointments at the University of Munich and the National Monuments Authority.

Hinrich Middeldorpf (1788–1861) was a scholar of linguistics and religious studies. After studying at the University of Göttingen, he spent his career at the University of Breslau from circa 1813 until 1861.
